overview: Rainbow AI is a WhatsApp AI assistant for Pelangi Capsule Hostel & Southern Homestay. It handles guest inquiries, booking workflows, and multi-turn conversations via Baileys WebSocket. The focus is on reliability, response quality, and intent classification accuracy.
goals: Improve intent classification accuracy for booking and inquiry intents
Enhance conversation context handling for multi-turn dialogues
Add better fallback responses when AI confidence is low
Improve the booking workflow steps in workflows.json
Prioritize reliability and response quality over new features
Enforce strict business profile separation â€” each profile's data files must only contain content specific to that business, with zero contamination from other profiles
Fix data-makan and data-southern profiles which currently contain copy-pasted Pelangi Capsule Hostel content
Enhance multilingual support - complete Tamil coverage, language preference UI
Improve production readiness - liveness probes, graceful shutdown, monitoring
Optimize performance - cache language preferences, batch DB inserts
Improve user experience - webchat loading states, language selector

epics.title: Intent Classification Accuracy
epics.description: Improve how the system classifies incoming messages into the correct intent categories, especially for booking and inquiry intents.

epics.title: Multi-Turn Conversation Context
epics.description: Enhance the system's ability to track and use conversation context across multiple turns of dialogue.

epics.title: Fallback & Confidence Handling
epics.description: Improve responses when the AI has low confidence or cannot classify an intent reliably.

epics.title: Booking Workflow Improvements
epics.description: Improve the booking workflow steps, transitions, and validation logic in workflows.json and related pipeline code.

epics.title: Test Suite Reliability
epics.description: Fix failing tests and improve test coverage for core intent and conversation logic.

epics.title: Business Profile Separation
epics.description: Ensure strict data isolation between all business profiles. Each profile's data files (knowledge.json, intents.json, intent-keywords.json, routing.json, templates.json, workflows.json) must contain ONLY content specific to that business. No profile may contain identifiers, addresses, credentials, pricing, or intents belonging to a different business.

userStories.title: Drain BullMQ Workers on Graceful Shutdown

userStories.title: Batch Fire-and-Forget DB Inserts in Intent Classifier
userStories.description: 10 separate sequential DB inserts per message. Batch with Promise.allSettled() to reduce pool pressure.
acceptanceCriteria: Failed inserts logged with structured error

_phaseI.diagnosisBlock:
## Current State

The intent-classifier.ts file contains 9 fire-and-forget DB operations scattered throughout the function, each with `.catch()` handlers:

1. Line 248: `db.insert(rainbowLowconfMessages)` 
2. Line 259: `db.insert(hardCaseQueue)`
3. Line 270: `db.insert(intentAnalytics)`
4. Line 278: `recordIntentLatency()`
5. Line 283: `recordTurnConfidence()`
6. Line 287: `logClassificationDecision()`
7. Line 296: `trackIntentPrediction()`
8. Line 315: `db.insert(escalationQueue)`
9. Line 342: `recordUtteranceGap()`

These are currently fired independently with no coordination, causing them to stress the DB pool sequentially.

## Problem Identified

Each fire-and-forget operation is independent, putting separate load on the PostgreSQL connection pool. When multiple messages arrive in quick succession, the pool gets exhausted. By batching with `Promise.allSettled()`, all operations can start concurrently, reducing peak pool pressure and improving overall throughput.

## Planned Changes

1. Create a `batchFireAndForgetInserts()` function that collects all DB operations into an array
2. Replace individual `.catch()` handlers with structured error logging inside the batch function
3. Call `Promise.allSettled()` on the batch to run all operations concurrently
4. Add test to verify batch execution
